title: Ye Servants of the Lord
description: Ye Servants of the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 277, “I Say unto You, Watch!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye ser-vants of the Lord! Each in your of-fice wait, Ob-ser-vant of His heav-enly word, And watch-ful at His gate.

lines: Let all your lamps be bright,
Gird up your loins, as in His sight;
And while we speak, He's near:
Mark the first signal of His hand,
He shall his Lord with rapture see,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
